chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from Muhammad ibn Isa from Muhammad ibn 'Arafah said:

I heard Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to say: 'When my nation becomes negligent in enjoining good and forbidding evil, let them anticipate a punishment from Allah, the Exalted.'

key_terms.تَوَاكَلَتِ: became negligent/lax in performing a duty
key_terms.وَالنَّهْيَ عَنِ الْمُنْكَرِ: and forbidding evil/prohibiting what is wrong

ai.seo_question: What is the consequence for the Muslim community if they neglect enjoining good and forbidding evil?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this narration links the spiritual health of the community directly to the active practice of *al-amr bi-l-ma'ruf wa al-nahy 'an al-munkar*. Imam al-Rida (AS) emphasizes that collective negligence in this duty invites *waqi'ah* (a calamity or plague), reflecting the Shia scholarly view that social justice is a prerequisite for divine favor. This serves as a practical warning that internal moral decay precedes external divine retribution.
